title: Probing Social Identity Bias in Chinese LLMs with Gendered Pronouns and Social Groups
findings: In the analysis of social identity biases across various Chinese social groups using the Qwen3-8B-Base model, the 'Religion' category showed a trend towards ingroup solidarity and outgroup hostility (odds ratios > 1). However, these findings were not statistically significant, as the confidence intervals were wide and crossed the 1.0 mark, indicating no definitive bias was detected for this specific category under the experimental conditions.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured social identity bias, specifically ingroup solidarity (more positive sentiment for 'we' statements) and outgroup hostility (more negative sentiment for 'they' statements), in text generated by LLMs when prompted about various social groups, including religious affiliations.
